rubrics.criterion: After the patch, document identity (title + ID) moves through the frontmatter/fs/fts pipeline as one encapsulated record — an existing metadata record, a newly defined record type, or the entity that carries it — and no function or method signature in those packages exchanges document identity as two parallel title/ID string parameters.
rubrics.rationale: This is the central request of the task prompt: the refactoring must reintroduce an abstraction that owns document identity, which is exactly what the pre-existing metadata record provided before it was unwrapped.

rubrics.criterion: The fs tree-node types (sections and groups) keep identity in one encapsulated place — a stored metadata record/reference or an equivalent identity-bearing record — instead of two detached string fields, so a node's identity has a single owner rather than two parallel primitives.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt explicitly points at the node shape ('the tree nodes no longer keep... two detached strings'), so storage-level encapsulation is a distinct outcome from signature-level encapsulation and both are required by this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Compound-identifier derivation — Entity.CompoundID in fs and the index-time section slug in fts — reads identity through the encapsulated record or entity accessors rather than from bare title/ID strings, and the ID/title fallback used during derivation is applied to the record rather than re-implemented over loose strings.
rubrics.rationale: Both derivation sites were split into bare-string helpers during the unwrapping; a complete repair must restore derivation from the owned record without reinstating a string-level duplicate of the fallback rule.

rubrics.criterion: All identity handoff sites were migrated coherently: frontmatter parsing finalizes the record in one place, fs.walk stores parsed metadata on every group/section (including the identity-less inline group content section and side-note wiring), and the fts index entry point consumes the record — with no remaining call in these packages that threads title and ID as separate strings between pipeline-internal functions.
rubrics.rationale: A partial migration would leave the same data flowing loose at other boundaries; the pipeline has exactly three internal handoffs (parse, walk/store, index) and the instance requires all three to be consistent.

rubrics.criterion: The consumer boundary outside the document pipeline stays compatible on the record's own terms: fs.Entity.Meta() still yields the identity record (returning nil for identity-less nodes), so consumers such as the parts renderer keep obtaining titles, IDs, and compound identifiers through the same interface without being adapted to any new pair-passing shape.
rubrics.rationale: The injected shim kept external consumers compiling; a sound repair must preserve that contract from the record side, not by teaching consumers about disassembled strings.

rubrics.criterion: The migration is not left half-finished: the patch contains no pipeline-internal path that still extracts title and ID into separate string locals and threads them through the remaining construction or derivation calls.
rubrics.rationale: A common failure mode for this kind of refactor is encapsulating the visible entry points while leaf call sites keep unwrapping the record, which would leave the task's underlying problem in place.

rubrics.criterion: The bare-string identity scaffolding is removed or fully repurposed: after the patch no left-over helper exists whose purpose was to receive (title, id) as two strings — including the parse-time identity-defaults helper in frontmatter, the record-reassembly shim and the pair-taking section/group constructors in fs, and the pair-based fallback and compound-slug helpers in fts.
rubrics.rationale: These helpers exist only to route the unwrapped pair; keeping them (even unused) would preserve the problem's structure and signal an incomplete cleanup of the instance's own injected machinery.

rubrics.criterion: The repair leaves no new dead weight behind: no unused fields, parameters, wrapper functions, or compatibility shims that no remaining call path uses.
rubrics.rationale: Encapsulation refactors in this pipeline often leave orphaned guards or accessors behind; their absence keeps ownership unambiguous.

rubrics.criterion: Frontmatter parsing keeps its exact observable semantics: the ID still defaults from the title and is slugified once at parse time, files without frontmatter still yield the same nil-metadata signal, unterminated frontmatter still fails the same way, and blank trailing content still collapses identically.
rubrics.rationale: These semantics are the pipeline's contract (the nil signal and slugified ID are observable through Meta() and the search index) and must survive the refactoring untouched.

rubrics.criterion: The patch introduces no behavioral side effects: no change to slug tables, stop-word lists, tokenizer or specials handling, serialization constants, tree layout, or error messages — identity handling is refactored, not redefined.
rubrics.rationale: The observed outputs (walk results, slugs, index contents, serialized blob) must remain identical for equivalent trees; edits to these unrelated value tables and constants are the concrete withdrawal path for accidental behavior loss in this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The refactoring does not break the repository's stable API surface: the fs.Entity interface methods, the exported frontmatter entry points (ExtractFromLines/ExtractFromFile), and the exported fts entry points (New/AddSection/Serialize) keep their names and signatures.
rubrics.rationale: Rendering templates, the CLI, and other packages consume this exact surface; renames or signature changes there are out of scope for an internal encapsulation cleanup of the identity handoff.
